title: Common Literary Devices
text: Metaphor compares two things directly without 'like/as'. Simile compares using 'like' or 'as'. Personification gives human traits to non-human things. Imagery uses descriptive language to appeal to the senses.

title: Elements of Poetry
text: Poetry is commonly analyzed through theme (central message), tone (author's attitude), rhyme scheme, rhythm/meter, and imagery — how these elements work together shapes meaning.

title: Analyzing Prose
text: Prose analysis typically covers plot structure, characterization (how characters are developed), setting, point of view (first/third person), and theme.

title: Elements of Drama
text: Drama is analyzed through plot, character, dialogue, stage directions, and dramatic devices like soliloquy (a character speaking their thoughts aloud) and dramatic irony (audience knows something characters don't).

title: Structuring a Literary Essay
text: A strong literary essay states a clear thesis in the introduction, supports it with evidence (quotes/references) and analysis in body paragraphs, and ties the argument together in the conclusion.

title: Theme vs Topic
text: A topic is what a work is about on the surface (e.g. 'war'). A theme is the underlying message or insight the work conveys about that topic (e.g. 'war strips away human dignity').
